speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: asked	the Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) whether he can provide an update on (i) the enhanced tracking efforts for international students who are receiving tuition grants in our polytechnics and publicly-funded universities; (ii) the number of international students who have not served their grant obligation upon graduation to date and the amount of tuition grants given to them; and (iii) the number of these students who have not served their grant obligation for more than three years after graduation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Over the past few years, we have put in place a number of measures to ensure bond fulfilment by tuition grant holders.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: At the start of their freshman year, all international students on tuition grants are briefed on the terms and conditions of the Tuition Grant Scheme, as well as the consequences of defaulting on their service obligations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They are also reminded of their obligations in their final year, just prior to graduation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOE is also working with other Government agencies to track the bond service records of the graduates closely.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It would not be accurate to say this entire minority is in default.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Let us take 2012, since the Member asked for the number of defaulters three years after graduation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Of the remaining 16%, we tracked them and found that some are working in Singapore but we do not have their employment records.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Some others are furthering their studies but did not go through the deferment procedures.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These should not be viewed in the same light as individuals who knowingly and willingly decide not to fulfil their service obligations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOE has sharpened the deterrent measures against defaulters to send a strong signal to deter would-be defaulters.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: First, are there any of such students who are classified as not contactable anymore?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The second question is, what is MOE going to do about these non-contactable students?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I find it strange that they are not deemed in default of their grant obligation.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The last question is, how many international students have been taken to task to date for not fulfilling their tuition grant obligations?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We try to reach out to them, there is no response, you cannot locate them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Over the years, the numbers that we can contact to ascertain their situation to see whether they are working, have been improving.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Slowly, we are able to contact more and more.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If some of them are really non-contactable, they will be considered in default.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for what then is the active action taken against them, as I have mentioned earlier, serious, adverse consequences, if they ever try to apply to enter or reside in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As you know, if you apply for work pass or Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP), the answer is a binary one – yes or no.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Member can infer what "adverse, serious consequences" means.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: The Acting Minister still has not answered the last question.
